title: Enterprise supplier onboarding playbook + vendor risk checklist to support pricing experiments
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Problem: Enterprise customers and prospects repeatedly request completed SOC2 artifacts, insurance limits, and vendor-portal onboarding before we can run procurement/PO-based pricing pilots. This slows sales cycles and makes pricing/packaging experiments with large accounts hard to execute.

Goal: Create a lightweight supplier onboarding playbook and vendor risk checklist that (1) standardizes the SOC2/insurance/portal deliverables we can provide, (2) maps those deliverables to pricing experiment stages (trial, pilot, PO, reserved capacity), and (3) produces a simple customer-facing package and an internal intake flow for Legal, Security, and Finance.

Deliverables: 
- Customer-facing "SOC2 & Onboarding" PDF kit with redacted artifacts and a clear list of what we share at each lifecycle stage.
- Internal vendor-risk checklist for Sales/Account Execs + Solutions Engineers (SOC2 evidence mapping, vendor portal invite steps, insurance thresholds, data residency controls).
- Onboarding playbook for pilots that ties required artifacts to pricing tiers and contract language snippets (pilot NDA -> PO -> reserved capacity SOW).
- A reusable intake form (Google/Form) that Sales submits to trigger Legal/Security review with auto-tags for risk level.
- Updated enterprise contract template snippets for typical procurement asks (proof of SOC2, subprocessor list, indemnity/insurance language).

Acceptance criteria: 
1) Legal and Security sign-off on the checklist and template snippets.
2) One live pilot executed using the playbook with Sales reporting >20% faster procurement milestone time compared to last quarter baseline.
3) Customer-facing kit uploaded to Drive and a canonical link added to Sales playbook.
4) Intake form creates a ticket in Legal queue with required artifacts attached.

Stakeholders: Sales (enterprise), Legal, InfoSec, Finance, Solutions Engineering, PMM, Engineering (security/infrastructure).

Risks/Trade-offs: 
- Over-sharing SOC2 artifacts increases maintenance burden; the playbook must standardize what to redact and how to rotate artifacts.
- Adding stricter insurance thresholds will slow pilots but reduce org risk; we will recommend minimal thresholds for pilots and higher limits for committed Reserved contracts.
- Creating a formal vendor portal might require infra work; interim approach uses signed links and controlled Drive folders.

Next steps: 
1) Run a 2-week discovery with Legal/InfoSec to agree scope and redaction rules (owner: Miguel).
2) Draft customer kit and template snippets (owner: Aisha).
3) Build intake form and small Zapier workflow to create tickets for Legal (owner: Ops).
4) Pilot the playbook with 2 enterprise prospects this quarter and collect timing metrics.

Related artifacts: Drive: https://drive.redwood/example/enterprise-onboarding-kit (draft), GitHub: https://github.com/redwood-inference/contracts/pull/402 (template diffs).
